purpose: A method for reasoning about the machine families that actually make a fully-fashioned sweater for a micro D2C knitwear brand sourcing in Ludhiana — what each family (computerised flat/V-bed, whole-garment, circular, the linker, finishing) does, its gauge range and role, the load-bearing fact that the knitting machine's value lives in its program not its metal and that the linker not the knitter caps a small line's daily output, and the resulting subcontract-vs-buy-used-vs-build decision — without ever stating a fabricated named-firm price, throughput or lead-time as fact.
assumptions: no landed vendor quotes are supplied; every price, MOQ, throughput and lead-time band is a labeled [ESTIMATE] with a stated method, basis and confidence, never a fake-precise figure presented as [FACT] for any named machine builder

the user is a deliberately tiny, fast-iterating acrylic/acrylic-blend capsule brand selling D2C in California/Turlock and sourcing knit-link-finish capacity through the Ludhiana job-work mesh, not a volume manufacturer

vendor identities, the 2025 Stoll/KARL MAYER flat-knit exit, HSN heading 8447, Groz-Beckert needle supply and the open/academic software-layer research are cited public [FACT]; their exact prices and dates carry their own tag
machine-to-dealer and supplier links (Ludhiana dealers, Groz-Beckert as needle supplier) are public-existence facts, not confirmed contracts for this brand unless a source states the relationship
throughput, capacity and cost-structure bands are order-of-magnitude planning priors drawn from industry-lore and vendor literature, not audited per-machine logs
exclusions: stating a fabricated dollar figure for a specifically named machine builder (Shima, Stoll, Cixing, Steiger) as fact rather than as a labeled estimate band
warp knitting (tricot/raschel) economics beyond naming it so it is not confused with weft/flat knitting (mostly outside shaped sweaters)
the yarn-side, finishing-chemistry, QC, brand and unit-economics deep-dives owned by the other specialists (T2, T6, T5, T7, T9) except where a machine decision straddles into them
a committed cost model or pro forma for an owned line (that is rebuilt bottom-up against a real Ludhiana unit in T4) — this models the machine decision, not the financial plan
tax, import-licensing and IP-legal advice for a specific purchase; this models the family landscape and the make-vs-buy decision, not a specific filing or transaction

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every money, capacity, throughput and lead-time figure in this KB: a reasoned band with stated method, basis and confidence carrying the literal word estimate, never a fake-precise figure presented as fact for any named machine builder; tidy single anchors are decision-framing illustrations downgraded to wide bands.

A sweater whose panels are knit to final shape by stitch increase/decrease (minimal waste, clean shaped edges) and then joined by linking; the core construction this machine chain centres on, distinct from cut-and-sew.

Two opposed needle beds that knit flat panels back-and-forth and shape them by increasing/decreasing stitches; the computerised versions (Shima, Stoll, Cixing-class) are the core fully-fashioned sweater technology.

A machine class that knits the entire garment in one piece with no panels and no linking at all; strategically it deletes the linker bottleneck but is the most expensive class with the steepest programming, a later volume decision.

The seaming machine that joins fully-fashioned panels edge-to-edge loop-to-loop for the flat, near-invisible, stretchy seam that defines a quality FF sweater; an eyesight-intensive, hand-skilled, piece-rate step that sets a small line's daily capacity, not the knitting.

Needles per inch on the bed (E7 = 7GG); the master fineness variable that must match yarn count and dictates machine, knit time and price tier, from ~3GG chunky to ~12GG fine (the right tier for warm-California elevated basics) to 14-18GG near-jersey.

The load-bearing fact that a computerised knitting machine's value lives in its vendor-locked knit-CAD program (needle actions, FF shaping, racking, carrier moves) far more than in its comparatively commoditised iron, which is why the programmer, not the machine, is the binding constraint.

The scarce, winnable, machine-specific skill that translates a design into a runnable machine program on a vendor-locked toolchain (Shima SDS-ONE APEX / APEXFiz vs Stoll M1plus / knitelligence); a harder constraint to acquire than the machine itself.

KARL MAYER (which acquired Stoll in 2020) decided in early 2025 to discontinue the STOLL flat-knitting machine business; the Reutlingen plant closed 31 Oct 2025, China production ended Dec 2025, with spares/service continuing only via the Obertshausen warehouse — narrowing new-build to Shima plus Chinese and deepening the used pool.

The dense agglomeration of spinners, knitters, linkers, finishers and machine dealers within reach in Ludhiana that lets a tiny brand subcontract knit+link+finish step by step; the one infrastructure moat that suits small, fast, varied capsule runs and keeps capital free for design and CAC.

nodes.definition: Establish the three machine families plus finishing that a fully-fashioned sweater passes through, because the make-vs-buy boundary sits in a different place for each. (1) The flat-bed/V-bed knitting machine knits and shapes panels — the core sweater technology, with whole-garment as a seamless sub-family that deletes linking. (2) Circular knitting knits a fast jersey tube for later cut-and-sew — high throughput, cheap per metre, no shaping, more casual, not the primary FF path. (3) The linker joins panels loop-to-loop and is the throughput bottleneck. (4) Finishing (steam press/boarding/wash/soften) turns a harsh off-machine panel into retail product. The load-bearing point: the linker, not the knitter, caps daily output, and the knitting machine's value lives in its program not its metal [FACT — family roles; SCOPE_GLOSSARY S3].

nodes.definition: Establish the computerised flat-bed (V-bed) machine as the core fully-fashioned sweater technology the whole chain centres on. Two opposed needle beds knit flat panels back-and-forth and shape them by increasing/decreasing stitches — knitting each panel to final shape with minimal waste, the defining FF move. It also transfers stitches for ribs, cables, pointelle and other structures, and works a wide gauge span. The computerised versions come from Shima Seiki (Japan) and Stoll (Germany), plus the fast-rising Chinese tier led by Cixing [FACT — vendor identities; SCOPE_GLOSSARY S3]. This is the machine every downstream cost, throughput and make-vs-buy judgment is built around, and the one whose program (not metal) carries its value.

nodes.definition: Define the whole-garment/seamless sub-family — Shima WHOLEGARMENT and Stoll knit&wear — which knits the entire garment in one piece, no panels, no linking at all. Strategically it is huge because it kills the linker bottleneck (the step that sets a small line's daily capacity), and it has near-zero cut waste. But it is the most expensive class with the steepest programming (a full 3D integral build), is slower per garment (~6-15 garments/machine/shift, [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]), and demands the most skilled programmer. Its strategic value lives entirely in deleting linking. For a capsule brand it is a later/volume trade study, never a launch move.

nodes.definition: Define circular knitting: a cylinder knits a continuous jersey tube fast for later cut-and-sew. It is not the primary path for shaped fully-fashioned sweaters, but it is relevant when a specific style is cut-and-sew jersey (e.g. a lightweight warm-California layer) where shaping is not needed and volume/cost dominate. Knowing it keeps the FF cost-and-quality story honest by naming the cheaper, lower-quality counterpoint to flat-knit FF.

It is not a bottleneck the way linking is, but rushed finishing shows directly as measurement and appearance defects, so a capsule brand subcontracting knit+link+finish must still gate finishing quality even though it does not own the step. nodes.definition: Establish that building your own knitting machine is the single highest-confidence do-not in this segment [ESTIMATE: engineering+business judgment, HIGH]. nodes.definition: Establish the binding constraint as human skill, not hardware, with two faces. For an AI-design brand specifically, the whole pipeline assumes someone can translate an AI design into a runnable program; if that programmer is scarce locally the pipeline stalls at the exact hand-off it depends on, which is why design-to-program AI assist is the highest-value AI investment. conflict_axes.description: Panelled flat-knit must staff the linker bottleneck while whole-garment deletes linking at the highest capital and steepest programming; a plan can over-weight either.
poles: staff the linker on panelled FF
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to panelled FF with staffed linking at launch; treat whole-garment's no-linking upside as a later volume trade study

conflict_axes.name: knitter_capacity_vs_linker_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: The faster knitting machine tempts sizing a line off machine count while the slower linker is the true daily ceiling.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always size the line off the linker ceiling and the programmer constraint, with machines feeding that ceiling

conflict_axes.name: program_value_vs_metal_value
conflict_axes.description: The machine's value lives in its vendor-locked program, but a buyer can fixate on the metal price and under-invest in the program and programmer.
poles: invest in the program and programmer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the program and programmer as the value-carrying asset; buy iron used and cheap, fund the program

conflict_axes.name: buy_used_vs_buy_new
conflict_axes.description: The deep used pool offers the same capability far below new, but used carries condition and parts diligence; new is rarely justified.
poles: buy used from the deep pool
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy used (Chinese/Cixing-class first) by default; reserve new for a volume/quality-benchmark purchase only

conflict_axes.name: build_own_vs_buy_and_program
conflict_axes.description: Build-your-own tempts a brand whose edge is product and AI, but the core kinematic chain is supplier-defended physics; buy-and-program wins decisively.
poles: buy and program an existing one
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy-and-program always; building is the highest-confidence do-not given Groz-Beckert needles and software-only research

conflict_axes.name: ai_real_leverage_vs_ai_hype
conflict_axes.description: AI genuinely multiplies the programmer and improves uptime and QC, but AI-builds-the-machine and AI-replaces-the-programmer/linker are hype/overstated.
poles: bet on AI autonomy over the machine
use AI as a software/data/vision multiplier
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: point AI at design-to-program assist, predictive maintenance and vision QC; treat machine-build and full-replacement claims as hype

conflict_axes.name: own_parts_periphery_vs_core_chain
conflict_axes.description: Reverse-engineering and 3D-printing save real uptime money on the periphery, but cloning the core kinematic chain destroys money and adds IP exposure.
poles: make own parts across the machine
make only periphery and maintenance parts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: periphery and maintenance yes, core kinematic chain never; cloning selection/firmware/knit-CAD is barred

conflict_axes.name: single_price_anchor_vs_wide_band
conflict_axes.description: A tidy single figure like a ~$15k used Chinese machine is decision-framing illustration, not a quote, and can drive a premature commit.
poles: commit on a single price anchor
hold a wide labeled band and get a landed quote
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat every single anchor as a wide LOW-MED [ESTIMATE] and require a real landed quote before any cost model commits

edge_cases.description: A line is sized off knitting-machine count and the slower linkers become the real bottleneck
edge_cases.trigger: capacity planned from machine throughput rather than the linker ceiling
edge_cases.mitigation: size the line off the linker ceiling and programmer constraint, with machines feeding that ceiling

edge_cases.description: A brand buys a used machine before any repeating program fills it, the programmer and the linkers
edge_cases.trigger: a buy on optimistic forecast rather than proven sustained volume
edge_cases.mitigation: stay subcontract until one repeating program at sustained volume fills the machine, programmer and linkers

edge_cases.description: A would-be machine-build budget is allocated against the core kinematic chain
edge_cases.trigger: a build-cheap myth treats needle bed/cams/selection/firmware as skippable
edge_cases.mitigation: buy-and-program a sub-$20k used machine; build-never, because Groz-Beckert makes the needles even for Shima and Stoll

edge_cases.description: A machine is acquired but the programmer hand-off is unsolved and the iron sits dead
edge_cases.trigger: iron bought while the scarce CAD/flat-knit programmer is not contracted
edge_cases.mitigation: rent/contract the scarce programmer and fund the CAD seat before or with any machine

edge_cases.description: A tidy single price anchor is quoted as a machine cost rather than a wide labeled band
edge_cases.trigger: a ~$15k used Chinese machine illustration is cited as a price
edge_cases.mitigation: label the anchor a wide LOW-MED [ESTIMATE] and require a real landed quote before committing a cost model

edge_cases.description: A machine cost model omits the HSN 8447 duty and the install/power/spares hidden lines
edge_cases.trigger: a sticker price is used as the landed cost
edge_cases.mitigation: gross the quote up by ~7.5% BCD + 18% IGST under HSN 8447 and add install, power, spares and ex-Stoll service

edge_cases.description: An ex-Stoll used machine is bought without pricing the Obertshausen-only parts-and-service risk
edge_cases.trigger: a post-2025 ex-Stoll buy ignores the discontinued service channel
edge_cases.mitigation: treat ex-Stoll parts-and-service via Obertshausen as a real diligence item and price it into the buy

edge_cases.description: An 'AI builds the machine' or 'no programmer needed' plan is taken at face value
edge_cases.trigger: AI hype is read as solving metrology, cams, selection or replacing the programmer
edge_cases.mitigation: point AI at design-to-program assist, predictive maintenance and vision QC only; AI does not fabricate iron or replace the programmer

edge_cases.description: A cited vision-QC accuracy is treated as a guarantee on the brand's acrylic/blend knits
edge_cases.trigger: a ~91-96% dataset-specific figure is read as transferable
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the accuracy as dataset-specific and have T5 validate vision QC on real samples of the brand's knits

edge_cases.description: Own-parts work drifts from the periphery into cloning the core kinematic chain
edge_cases.trigger: a maintenance project slides from a bracket into needle-selection or firmware cloning
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the periphery-yes core-chain-never line and avoid cloning selection/firmware/knit-CAD for IP/legal exposure

edge_cases.description: A whole-garment machine is bought at capsule scale before the volume justifies its capital and programming
edge_cases.trigger: the no-linking upside is chased at launch rather than at proven volume
edge_cases.mitigation: treat whole-garment as a later volume trade study; default to panelled FF with staffed linking at launch

edge_cases.description: A shaped sweater is routed to circular cut-and-sew, absorbing avoidable waste and a more casual result
edge_cases.trigger: circular's speed and low cost pull a shaped style off the FF flat-knit path
edge_cases.mitigation: route shaped sweaters to flat-knit FF and reserve circular for genuinely cut-and-sew jersey styles

workflow.action: Map the machine families and their roles
workflow.description: State flat-bed/V-bed, whole-garment, circular, the linker and finishing and what each does
workflow.gate: all families are named with their step-role and the linker-caps-output and program-over-metal headline are stated

workflow.action: Establish the flat-bed core and its sub-family
workflow.description: Anchor on the two-bed FF technology and name the whole-garment seamless variant
workflow.gate: the two-bed FF shaping move, the vendor identities and the whole-garment variant are stated

workflow.action: Establish the linker as the bottleneck
workflow.description: Define loop-to-loop linking and why it not knitting sets the daily ceiling
workflow.gate: the loop-to-loop seam, the eyesight/hand-skill/piece-rate nature and the capacity-setting role are stated

workflow.action: Map gauge ranges to product tiers
workflow.description: Define GG/E and the coarse-to-fine product map matched to yarn count
workflow.gate: GG/E is defined, the gauge map is given, and the 12GG warm-California tier and gauge-yarn matching are named

workflow.action: State that value lives in the program not the metal
workflow.description: Establish the knit-CAD program as the value-carrying asset on vendor-locked toolchains
workflow.gate: the program-as-asset point, the vendor-locked non-portability and the link to the programmer constraint are stated

workflow.action: Lay down the labeled-estimate price bands
workflow.description: State per-class new/used bands as wide [ESTIMATE]s with a get-a-landed-quote rule
workflow.gate: every band carries the [ESTIMATE] label and a confidence and the single-anchor-is-not-a-quote warning is present

workflow.action: Add the India import duty and hidden costs
workflow.description: Gross the price up by HSN 8447 BCD+IGST plus install/power/spares/ex-Stoll service
workflow.gate: HS heading 8447, the ~7.5% BCD + 18% IGST working assumption and the hidden lines are stated

workflow.action: Account for the Stoll exit and the used pool
workflow.description: Carry the 2025 Stoll exit as fact and the deep-and-deepening used pool it feeds
workflow.gate: the cited 2025 exit, the Shima-plus-Chinese narrowing and the used-pool-deepens consequence are stated

workflow.action: Set subcontract as the launch default
workflow.description: Subcontract knit+link+finish into the mesh and own only design, brand and a sampling hand-flat
workflow.gate: the subcontract bundle, the agglomeration-is-infrastructure logic and the owned-line reality as a labeled illustration are stated

workflow.action: Set the buy-used threshold and the build-never verdict
workflow.description: Buy used Chinese-first at proven volume; build your own machine never
workflow.gate: the proven-volume buy trigger, Chinese-class-first, and the build-never core-chain/Groz-Beckert/software-only verdict are stated

workflow.action: Name the programmer bottleneck and the AI line
workflow.description: Establish the CAD programmer and linker as the binding constraint and point AI at the software layer
workflow.gate: the CAD/flat-knit programmer as binding constraint, the linker second face, and the real-vs-hype AI line are stated

workflow.action: Compose the merged verdict and capacity plan
workflow.description: Intersect families, costs, market and bottleneck into the make-vs-buy verdict and a linker-sized capacity plan
workflow.gate: the subcontract/buy-used/build-never/AI-at-software verdict, the landed-quote precondition and the linker-and-programmer-sized capacity plan are stated

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any price, throughput or lead-time claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no landed quote is in hand, so a band may never be presented as a fact for a named machine builder
dominance_rules.trigger: any money, capacity or lead-time figure is attached to a machine class or named builder
dominance_rules.action: tag it [ESTIMATE] with method and confidence (or [FACT]/[UNKNOWN] where that is true) and require a landed quote before a cost model commits

dominance_rules.rule: The programmer and linker dominate the machine in any capacity or buy decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the binding constraint is human skill, not the iron, so the cheapest machine is dead without the program hand-off and the linker
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan sizes capacity or justifies a buy off the knitting machine alone
dominance_rules.action: size off the linker ceiling and the programmer constraint and secure both before owning iron

dominance_rules.rule: Buy-used dominates buy-new which dominates build
dominance_rules.rationale: the deep used pool offers the same capability far cheaper, new is rarely justified, and building the core chain is the highest-confidence do-not
dominance_rules.action: default to used Chinese-first, reserve new for a benchmark purchase, and never build the core machine

dominance_rules.rule: Subcontract dominates owning iron at capsule scale
dominance_rules.rationale: a tiny iterating brand rarely hits the utilisation an owned line needs, and the mesh is the infrastructure
dominance_rules.trigger: an owned line is proposed before a repeating program at sustained volume exists
dominance_rules.action: stay subcontract until one program at volume fills the machine, programmer and linkers

dominance_rules.rule: The program dominates the metal in judging machine value
dominance_rules.rationale: the value lives in the vendor-locked knit-CAD program, not the comparatively commoditised iron
dominance_rules.trigger: a machine is judged on its metal price alone
dominance_rules.action: weigh the program and the programmer access, not just the iron, and buy the metal used and cheap

dominance_rules.rule: Real AI leverage dominates AI hype on machines
dominance_rules.rationale: AI multiplies the programmer and improves uptime and QC but does not fabricate iron or replace the programmer/linker
dominance_rules.trigger: a strategy rests on AI building the machine or removing the programmer/linker
dominance_rules.action: point AI at design-to-program assist, predictive maintenance and vision QC and reject the machine-build and full-replacement claims

dominance_rules.rule: Periphery own-parts dominate core-chain own-parts (which are barred)
dominance_rules.rationale: periphery and maintenance own-parts save real uptime money while the core kinematic chain destroys money and adds IP exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: an own-parts or reverse-engineering effort targets a part
dominance_rules.action: make periphery and maintenance parts only and never the needle bed/needles/cams/selection/firmware/knit-CAD

dominance_rules.rule: Landed quotes dominate single price anchors
dominance_rules.rationale: tidy single figures are decision-framing illustrations, not quotes, and used capital-goods price is condition-specific
dominance_rules.trigger: a single price anchor is used to commit a cost model
dominance_rules.action: treat the anchor as a wide [ESTIMATE] and get a real landed quote (machine + freight + duty + install) first

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the [ESTIMATE] label and confidence when a price or throughput band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fake-precise machine figure circulating as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Secure and fund the CAD/flat-knit programmer before or with any machine acquisition
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a bought machine sitting as dead iron because the program hand-off was unsolved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the line off the linker ceiling, not the knitting machine, from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an owned line built around idle iron and starved or over-staffed linkers

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm one repeating program at sustained volume before buying used iron
anti_rework_rules.prevents: owning a machine and its payroll for a style whose repeat volume never materialises

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gross every machine quote up by HSN 8447 duty and the install/power/spares hidden lines in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cost model committed on a sticker price that understates the true landed cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the periphery-yes core-chain-never own-parts line from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a maintenance project drifting into core-chain cloning that destroys money and adds IP exposure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep AI scoped to the software/data/vision layers and validate vision-QC accuracy on the brand's knits
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a strategy built on AI-builds-the-machine hype or a dataset-specific accuracy assumed transferable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat the build-your-own-machine option as a settled do-not, not a re-opened trade study
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-litigating a ~$2M-10M+/3-7yr build that a sub-$20k used machine already beats

iteration_protocol.trigger: real landed used-machine quotes (Chinese vs Shima/Stoll, by gauge/condition, + freight/duty/install) are obtained
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled price bands with confirmed landed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: job-work rates for knitting and linking per piece are confirmed on the ground
iteration_protocol.action: re-decide the subcontract-vs-buy-used economics and the capacity plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: local availability and cost of a CAD/flat-knit programmer vs operators is confirmed
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the programmer bottleneck and the AI-assisted-vs-hired split

iteration_protocol.trigger: AI design-to-program autonomy or vision-QC accuracy is tested on the brand's acrylic/blend fabrics
iteration_protocol.action: move the affected AI claims between real and hype and update the programmer-relaxation read

iteration_protocol.trigger: ex-Stoll parts/service cost and availability post-Reutlingen-closure becomes known
iteration_protocol.action: update the used-pool and ex-Stoll diligence read

iteration_protocol.trigger: the exact India BCD sub-heading rate or a 2025-26 budget change is confirmed at purchase
iteration_protocol.action: update the import-duty math and the landed-cost precondition

iteration_protocol.trigger: one style reaches sustained volume that justifies owning iron or a whole-garment trade study
iteration_protocol.action: cross the make-vs-buy boundary to buy-used and re-evaluate the whole-garment no-linking upside

priority_rationale: The machine-family map, the flat-bed core, the linker bottleneck, gauge and the program-over-metal point come first because every cost, throughput and make-vs-buy judgment depends on knowing what each family does and where its value and ceiling sit; the price bands, import duty, vendor tiers, Stoll exit and used-pool depth next, because they turn the families into a cost and market-structure picture; the sourcing decisions (subcontract, buy-used, build-never) and the programmer/AI/own-parts bottleneck nodes then apply that picture to the brand's actual choices; and the merged make-vs-buy verdict and the linker-and-programmer-sized capacity plan come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible subcontract-now, buy-used-at-volume, build-never, AI-at-the-software-layer call.
